text:
[LNUL.4.9] **`x is <subject>` / `x is not <subject>` — the total tag test.**
The operator tests the value's **tag** ([LNUL.9.1]'s discriminant) against a
**closed** set of subjects. It **must** answer `true` or `false` for a value of
any kind: it **must not** yield `null` and **must not** raise. `is not` is one
operator, not `not` applied to `is`.

**The subject set is closed and is not the type namespace.** A schema has no
representation of its own, so it is neither spellable as a subject nor
answerable by one. The twelve subjects are six **distinguished constants** and
six **tag names**:

| subject | `true` exactly when |
|---|---|
| `null` | the value is `null` |
| `true` / `false` | the tag is `Bool` **and** the value is that boolean |
| `inf` / `-inf` | the tag is `Float` **and** the value is that infinity |
| `NaN` | the tag is `Float` **and** the value is NaN |
| `Int` `Float` `Bool` `String` `Bytes` `Json` | the tag is that one, whatever the value |

**`false` in every other case**, including when the value is `null` and the
subject is not `null`.

**A constant tests tag and value; a tag name tests the tag alone.** So
`is Float` is `true` of `inf`, `-inf` and `NaN` alike, and `is Bool` is `true`
of `false`.

**A tag names a representation, not a declared type**, and an annotation riding
on a representation does not change it. A unit-typed value is an `Int` or a
`Float` carrying a compile-time dimension ([LUNI.4.1]); a `Time` is an `Int`
carrying an ingestion-fixed zone offset, and `[LTIM.1.1.1]` already orders,
compares and computes on its `utc_ns` alone. Each answers to the tag that
carries it:

| type | answers `true` to |
|---|---|
| `Time`, `Date`, `Duration` | `Int` — an epoch, day or nanosecond count ([LTIM.1.3.1]) |
| a unit-typed value | `Int` or `Float`, whichever its declared `storage` names |
| `Ratio`, a fact reference | nothing — `false` to all six |

**A value whose representation is none of the six answers `false` to all six.**
That is what makes the partition total without the subject set having to name
every type: a type reaches this operator only through the tag that carries it,
and a type no tag carries is invisible to it rather than an error.

**The answer is a function of the value alone.** An implementation **must**
answer alike for two values alike in representation, however each reached the
operator: a `Time` written by a clock and an epoch `Int` asserted by an
integrator into the same slot are indistinguishable here, even where the
implementation separates them internally. Provenance is not a tag.

**The tag is read before any value conversion.** This is what makes totality
achievable for a `Json` string leaf: the tag is on the term, so `is String`
answers without interning anything.

**Why totality is load-bearing.** A guard that could fail on the condition it
guards is not a guard. `[LNUL.4.1]`'s propagation makes every ordinary operator
yield `null` on a `null` operand, so absence cannot be branched on by
arithmetic or comparison; this operator is the one that can, and every stricter
disposition elsewhere rests on it never failing.

idris.name: Lnul_4_9__subject
idris.note: The twelve subjects as a closed type: the six distinguished constants and the six tag names, and no thirteenth.

idris.name: lnul_4_10__tag_test_of_a_trap_is_the_trap
idris.note: An operand that faults is the answer for every subject and either polarity: the operator itself never raises, and a fault in the operand has no value whose tag could be read.

idris.name: lnul_4_4__is_null_is_total
idris.note: The null subject: true or false on a value of any kind.

idris.name: lnul_4_9__constant_tests_the_value
idris.note: A constant tests tag AND value: is true is false of a Bool false and is false true of it; a constant of one tag is false of every value of another, quantified over that value.

idris.name: lnul_4_9__inf
idris.note: The inf subject's value test: the Float above zero that equals its own double, which only the positive infinity does.

idris.name: lnul_4_9__is
idris.note: The operator: is and, by its flag, is not as one operator; true or false for a value of any kind, never null; a fault in the operand stands.

idris.name: lnul_4_9__is_total
idris.note: Total for every subject and either polarity: on a value of any kind the answer is a Bool, never null and never a trap.

idris.name: lnul_4_9__nan
idris.note: The NaN subject's value test: the one value unequal to itself.

idris.name: lnul_4_9__neg_inf
idris.note: The -inf subject's value test: the Float below zero that equals its own double.

idris.name: lnul_4_9__null_answers_only_null
idris.note: False in every other case, the null value included: a null answers true to the null subject and false to each of the other eleven.

idris.name: lnul_4_9__tag_and_value
idris.note: The clause's first table over the fragment's six kinds (Int, Float, String, Bool, Json, null): a constant tests tag and value, a tag name the tag alone, false in every other case. Bytes is a tag no value of the fragment carries and answers false to every value. The second table -- Time, Date and Duration as Int, a unit-typed value as its storage, Ratio and a fact reference as none -- names representations the fragment does not model.

idris.name: lnul_4_9__tag_name_tests_the_tag_alone
idris.note: A tag name tests the tag alone, quantified over the value: is Float of every Float, the infinities and a NaN alike; is Int, is String, is Bool and is Json of every value of their tag.
